summary: A speed menu sits beside play on a video's transport: 0.25x, 0.5x, 1x, 1.5x, 2x, 4x and 8x. Sound keeps its pitch up to 2x and goes quiet above it, Shift-period and Shift-comma step the speed, and J/K/L show their speed in the same control.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open any recording.

try.do: Open a recording and look right of the Go to End button: the speed control reads 1x.
Click the speed control and pick 0.5x, then press Space. It plays at half speed and voices sound slower, not lower.
While it plays, pick 1.5x from the same menu. It changes speed where it is.
Pick 4x. The sound goes quiet and the control shows a struck-through speaker. Press Space to stop.
Press Shift-comma a few times, then Shift-period. The speed steps down and up the menu.
Click the timeline, press Home, then L three times. The control reads 4x while it runs; K stops it and the control goes back to your chosen speed.
Open Sequence in the menu bar: Play Faster and Play Slower sit under Play Forward.

evaluate: Is beside the play buttons where you expect a speed control, or would you look for it at the far right like YouTube's?
Does half speed sound right to you: slower, with voices at their own pitch?
Is the struck-through speaker on 4x and 8x enough to tell you why the sound went quiet?
Should picking a speed while stopped also start playing, or is waiting for Space right?
Do Shift-period and Shift-comma feel natural, or would you rather have a different key?
rough: 8x on the six minute reference edit does not keep up yet: at 8x the picture falls up to 185 frames behind (4x keeps up at every look, and so does 8x on the five minute Retina talk). This task stays open for it.

Starting 2x from rest on the five minute Retina talk once held a frame 4 behind at the first look, in 1 of 3 runs; every later look kept up. The same start at 4x and 8x now waits up to half a second for its first frame, which is silent; at 2x and below it does not wait, because the sound has already started.
No mock draws a speed control. It sits in the transport because the placement contract gives that row play controls (UX-PATTERNS placement contract, Transport row).

Shift-period and Shift-comma are a web player's keys: neither Premiere nor Final Cut gives a key to a speed menu, and Final Cut's own Shift-comma and Shift-period nudge, which Premiere does with Command-Shift-arrows here (UX-PATTERNS §7).
The checklist said J L L shows 4x; with Premiere's ladder J then L restarts at 1x forwards, so the walk checks L L L, which is the press that reaches 4x.
The speed is the window's own: every new window starts at 1x, it is not saved into the document, and Export never sees it.
